What is evaluated: Trivy and Grype on 22 standard and minimized container images
Unit reported: Total findings, unique CVEs, severity counts, overlap between scanners
Relation to this study: Keeps component/advisory identity and artifact occurrence separate, and shows that they lead to different conclusions about omitting a stage

What is evaluated: Reduction of false positives and inconsistencies among container scanners
Relation to this study: Measures which reference instances a reduction keeps or loses, rather than agreement between tools

What is evaluated: Deduplication and tracking of SAST findings across tools and code versions
Relation to this study: Separates incorrect associations from losses caused by discarding group members, at fixed snapshots

What is evaluated: LLM filtering of static-analysis alarms in an industrial setting (433 alarms)
Unit reported: False positives removed, recall, cost per alarm
Relation to this study: Counts lost true findings, latency and memory for local models, and checks explanations against the supplied code

What is evaluated: Stateful REST API fuzzing guided by predicted request categories
Relation to this study: Records whether each dynamic job reached the operation its reference requires

What is evaluated: LLM guidance to a human tester in Android dynamic testing
Unit reported: Test cases fully, partially or not discovered
Relation to this study: Concerns the removal of existing findings, not guidance to a tester

What is evaluated: Evidence-gated LLM review that holds cases when evidence is missing
Relation to this study: Applies a conservative fallback, then measures what is still lost

What is evaluated: A six-stage Jenkins pipeline with PHP analysis tools for a multi-tier web application on AWS provisioned with Terraform
Unit reported: Seconds per run and per stage; processor, memory and cost per run; reported issues; blocking rate
Relation to this study: Adds instance-level outcomes to the measurement of scanning cost
